new: ### E.1 Elementary lower bound and its scope Under the same assumptions and normalization, choose the trial field $\boldsymbol\phi=f_h(z)\mathbf e_i$, where $f_h(z)=z(h-z)/2$ for $0\le z\le h$ and is zero for $z\ge h$. The field is continuous and zero at $z=h$, belongs to $H^1$, has zero trace on all solid walls, including the vertical steps, and is periodic. It is weakly divergence free for either horizontal principal direction. The derivative jump at the internal interface does not prevent admissibility; a trial field need not satisfy the momentum equation. Define $a(\boldsymbol v,\boldsymbol w)=\int_\Omega\nabla\boldsymbol v:\nabla\boldsymbol w\,\mathrm dA$ and $\ell_i(\boldsymbol v)=\int_\Omega v_i\,\mathrm dA$. The weak formulation of Eq. (E1), together with Eq. (E2), gives $$ P K_i-\bigl[2\ell_i(\boldsymbol\phi)-a(\boldsymbol\phi,\boldsymbol\phi)\bigr] =a(\mathbf U-\boldsymbol\phi,\mathbf U-\boldsymbol\phi)\ge0. \tag{E7} $$ For this trial field, $\ell_i(\boldsymbol\phi)=a(\boldsymbol\phi,\boldsymbol\phi)=Ph^3/12$. Combining this result with Eq. (E6), the continuous conductance in either principal direction satisfies $$ L:=\frac{h^3}{12}\le K_i\le U_i:=K_i^{\rm mod}, \qquad i\in\{x,y\}. \tag{E8} $$ The lower bound equals the parallel-plate conductance obtained by retaining only the connected layer of thickness $h$ and imposing an additional zero-velocity constraint in the groove cavity; it does not describe the actual cavity velocity. It contains no groove-width dependence and cannot independently explain width effects. Among the 19 comparison geometries, the maximum upper-to-lower ratio $U_i/L$ is 63 along the grooves and approximately 1.984 across them. A narrower interval does not establish a specified point-prediction accuracy. Dimensional lower bounds differ with $h$; only normalization by each geometry's own $L$ gives a common left endpoint of 1. The 36 main 5 nm records, two added-gap records and eight refinement records give 46 distinct discrete records, all within their respective bounds. This is compatibility with the continuous bounds, rather than a substitute for the lower-bound proof or numerical-accuracy assessment. Separately, for only the 36 main 5 nm results from 18 geometries, with discrete conductance as denominator, the lower bound underestimates by an average of 58.2% along and 23.8% across the grooves; the local cubic law overestimates by 88.8% and 30.6%, respectively. In each direction the lower bound is closer for 11/18 geometries. This baseline comparison includes reference-grid effects and does not establish general predictive ability of the lower bound. ## References
